state: FORUM THREAD — 'Millbrook Lab Ops Bulletin Board' — Thread: 'Sorvall RX-7 centrifuge imbalance errors after relocation' — Started 12 March 2024. POST 1 — user 'chiara_b' (Chiara Bergstrom, lab manager, Whitfield Neuroscience Lab, Nordhaven University): Hi all, we moved our Sorvall RX-7 floor-model centrifuge from our old suite on the second floor of Corbin Hall to the new wet-lab wing last week. Ever since the move we are getting E-41 imbalance errors on roughly every third run, even with perfectly matched rotor loads. The unit ran clean for six years in the old location. The move was done by the university's contracted movers, not by us, and the unit was carried, never tipped, per the mover's paperwork. Rotor is the fixed-angle TA-10, same one we always used. Any ideas before I burn a service call budget line? POST 2 — user 'rotorjockey' (Gus Mahoney, facilities tech, Eastport State): Welcome to the club. E-41 on the RX-7 after a move is a classic. Nine times out of ten it is the vibration isolator pads under the feet. When the movers lift these units, the pads sometimes stay behind on the old floor or get re-seated crooked. Check that all four pads are present and the unit is sitting flat. I would put a spirit level on the top deck and confirm it reads level side to side and front to back. If the pads are missing, do not run the unit; the imbalance errors are the machine protecting itself and an uncorrected imbalance at speed can wreck the drive. POST 3 — user 'm_delacroix' (Marcel Delacroix, core facility director, Pell Institute): Agreed on the pads, but one more thing: the RX-7 has a transportation lock bolt under the front panel that is supposed to be removed after any move. If the movers did not remove it, the suspension cannot float and you will get phantom imbalance readings at any speed above about 3,000 rpm. The lock is a yellow knob under the lower front cover. Check the manual, section 7.2, 'Post-Relocation Checklist.' Also confirm the rotor seating: even a hairline of dust between the rotor taper and the spindle will give you the same fault. POST 4 — user 'chiara_b': Thanks both. Update: I checked the pads first thing this morning. All four pads are present and seated, and the unit is level within a quarter bubble on the spirit level. The yellow transportation lock bolt was still in place — the movers apparently never removed it. I removed it per section 7.2 of the manual. I then cleaned the rotor taper and the spindle with isopropyl and re-seated the rotor by hand, then ran a test spin at 4,000 rpm with a balanced load and got a clean run, no E-41. Ran two more test spins at 8,000 rpm, both clean. One question: do I need to log this as an incident with the university safety office? Nothing failed, no samples lost, just error codes. I arrived at approximately 09:05 and parked the van in the marked loading bay of Lot 12C with my hazard lights on. Campus Parking Regulation 14.3 states: 'A vehicle displaying hazard lights and actively engaged in loading or unloading of materials at a marked loading bay may remain for a period not exceeding thirty (30) minutes, provided the operator remains within the immediate vicinity of the vehicle.' I was parked in a marked loading bay. I displayed hazard lights. I was actively unloading cryogenic materials, an activity which regulation 14.3 is designed to accommodate, and which cannot be performed from a general parking space because the samples require the shortest possible outdoor exposure. I was present for approximately 21 minutes, from 09:05 to 09:26, well within the thirty-minute allowance. I remained in the immediate vicinity of the vehicle in the sense contemplated by the regulation, never proceeding beyond the ground-floor receiving corridor, which is visible from the loading bay through the corridor windows. state: EXCERPT OF ARBITRATOR'S FINAL AWARD AND PARTIAL OPINION — Millbrook Arbitration Association, Matter No. ARB-2023-4091 — Kestrel Dental Supply Company (Claimant) v. Nordhaven University Oral Microbiome Research Unit (Respondent) — Arbitrator: Hon. (Ret.) Marguerite Oyelaran. BACKGROUND. This matter arises from a Sponsored Research and Materials Supply Agreement dated 15 September 2021 between Kestrel Dental Supply Company ('Kestrel') and the Nordhaven University Oral Microbiome Research Unit ('the Unit'), a laboratory within the Nordhaven University School of Dentistry. The principal investigator of record under the Agreement is Dr. Farid Kowalski, Associate Professor of Oral Biology. The Agreement had a primary term of two years, commencing 15 September 2021 and ending 14 September 2023, subject to a single renewal option exercisable by Kestrel on sixty days' written notice before the end of the primary term. FINDINGS OF FACT. 1. Under the Agreement, Kestrel agreed to supply the Unit with consumable culturing media, sterile collection vials, and analytical reagents at no charge for the term, valued at approximately $34,000 per year, and to pay the Unit a sponsorship fee of $60,000 per year, payable in two equal installments on the first business day of January and the first business day of July. 2. Kestrel agreed to fund the sponsorship fee for the 2023 contract year. The January 2023 installment of $30,000 was paid on 3 January 2023 and received without dispute. The July 2023 installment of $30,000 was not paid. 3. On 12 May 2023, Kestrel's Director of Research Partnerships, Ms. Odette Ferreira, sent a letter to Dr. Kowalski stating that Kestrel was undergoing a corporate restructuring and would 'not be in a position to continue the partnership beyond the current calendar year.' The letter did not exercise the renewal option, did not state an intention to terminate the Agreement before the end of its term, and did not invoke any cure provision. 4. On 30 June 2023, Dr. Kowalski replied by email to Ms. Ferreira acknowledging the restructuring, stating that the Unit would complete the funded work through the end of the primary term, and asking for confirmation that the July installment would be paid. Ms. Ferreira did not reply. 5. The July 2023 installment remained unpaid as of 15 September 2023, the end of the primary term. The Unit filed its demand for arbitration on 2 October 2023, seeking the unpaid $30,000 installment plus costs. 6. During the summer of 2023, the Unit continued to order and receive consumable supplies from Kestrel under the Agreement. Kestrel continued to fulfill all such orders, its last shipment leaving its warehouse on 22 August 2023. 7. Kestrel asserted in its Answer that the Unit failed to deliver a final data package owed under Section 8.4 of the Agreement, which required the Unit to deliver a consolidated dataset and summary report within ninety days of the end of the primary term. The evidence shows that the Unit delivered the consolidated dataset on 10 December 2023 and the summary report on 12 December 2023, both within the ninety-day window, which ended 14 December 2023. Kestrel acknowledged receipt of both in an email dated 14 December 2023. ANALYSIS AND AWARD. Kestrel raised two defenses: first, that the May 2023 letter constituted notice of termination excusing further payment; second, that the Unit breached first by failing to deliver the final data package. As to the first defense, the May 2023 letter did not exercise the renewal option, did not terminate the Agreement, and did not invoke any cure provision. An expression of an intention not to continue beyond the current term is not a termination of the current term. The Agreement remained in force through 14 September 2023, and the July 2023 installment obligation matured during the term. As to the second defense, the Unit delivered the final data package within the ninety-day window ending 14 December 2023, and Kestrel acknowledged receipt. The defense therefore fails as to both breach and timing. AWARD. 1. Kestrel shall pay the Unit the unpaid July 2023 installment of $30,000 within thirty days of this Award. 2. Kestrel shall pay the Unit's arbitration costs, the fees of the Association having been shared equally during the proceeding. 3. All other claims and defenses are denied. 4. This Award is final and binding pursuant to Section 4.2 of the Agreement and the Millbrook Arbitration Act. Issued 8 February 2024. /s/ M. Oyelaran, Arbitrator.

state: COLLABORATION COMPLIANCE REVIEW REPORT — Fiscal Year 2023 — Prepared by the Office of Research Integrity and Compliance, Nordhaven University — Reviewed entity: Coastal Food Fermentation Research Laboratory (the 'Lab'), Principal Investigator Dr. Leila Lindqvist, Professor of Food Science — Industry partner: Tidewater Foods, Inc. — Review period: 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023 — Report reference ORIC-2024-017 — Approved 22 March 2024 — PART ONE: SCOPE AND METHOD. This review was conducted under the University's Industry Collaboration Compliance Policy (the 'Policy'), version 4.1, effective 1 August 2022. The review examined the Lab's documentation of its sponsored collaboration with Tidewater Foods, Inc. ('Tidewater'), covering five areas: financial disclosure, data ownership and access, publication rights, conflict of interest management, and materials handling. The review team inspected the sponsored research agreement dated 6 February 2023, twelve monthly progress reports, the Lab's electronic lab notebook exports, purchasing records, and the University's conflict-of-interest disclosure database. PART TWO: FINDINGS BY AREA. AREA 1 — FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE. Finding 1.1: The sponsored research agreement provides for total direct funding of $412,500 for the review period. University accounting records show receipt of $412,500, fully reconciled. COMPLIANT. Finding 1.2: The agreement obligates the Lab to purchase all fermentation consumables from Tidewater's catalog division unless an item is unavailable there. Purchasing records show 23 of 25 purchase orders were placed with the catalog division. Two purchase orders, totaling $3,180, were placed with Harbor Scientific Supply for items the review team verified as unavailable in the Tidewater catalog (a specialty pH microelectrode and a discontinued agar formulation). COMPLIANT, with a documentation note: the unavailability verification emails were not filed with the purchasing records but were retrieved from the Lab's shared mailbox during the review. AREA 2 — DATA OWNERSHIP AND ACCESS. Finding 2.1: The agreement grants Tidewater a non-exclusive license to project data and requires the Lab to deposit raw data in the University repository within six months of the project end date. The project end date is 31 December 2024; the deposit obligation matures on 30 June 2025 and is not yet due. NO FINDING REQUIRED. Finding 2.2: The review found that Dr. Lindqvist shared preliminary sensory panel spreadsheets with a Tidewater scientist, Ms. Rhea Calloway, via personal email on 14 and 28 March 2023, rather than through the project data portal required by Section 9.2 of the agreement. The spreadsheets contained only aggregated panel scores with no individual panelist identifiers. The Lab subsequently migrated all sharing to the portal as of 3 April 2023. NON-COMPLIANT (procedural, self-corrected before the review). AREA 3 — PUBLICATION RIGHTS. Finding 3.1: The agreement gives the Lab the right to publish project results after a 45-day Tidewater review window. The review team examined one manuscript, 'Volatile ester profiles in low-sodium fermentations,' submitted to the Journal of Applied Food Chemistry on 17 August 2023. The manuscript was delivered to Tidewater for review on 2 June 2023, returned with comments on 10 July 2023 (38 days later), and submitted 17 August 2023, after the window had closed. COMPLIANT. Finding 3.2: Tidewater requested a 30-day extension of the review window on 28 June 2023. Dr. Lindqvist declined the request in writing on 30 June 2023, citing the scheduled submission timeline. No further request was made. COMPLIANT. AREA 4 — CONFLICT OF INTEREST MANAGEMENT. Finding 4.1: Dr. Lindqvist's spouse, Tomasz Lindqvist, has been employed by Tidewater Foods as a flavor chemist since 2019, in a division unconnected to the collaboration. Dr. Lindqvist disclosed this relationship to the University's conflict-of-interest database on 20 January 2023, before the agreement was signed on 6 February 2023, and a management plan was put in place on 27 January 2023 under which Tomasz Lindqvist has no role in the project, no access to project data, and does not attend project meetings. The review team verified meeting attendance logs and data access logs; no access by Tomasz Lindqvist was found. COMPLIANT. AREA 5 — MATERIALS HANDLING. Finding 5.1: The agreement requires all project microbial strains to be stored in the Lab's dedicated minus-80 freezer bank with chain-of-custody logs. The review team traced all 17 project strains and found complete chain-of-custody records. COMPLIANT. Finding 5.2: On 9 October 2023, a sealed shipment of four Tidewater-supplied starter cultures arrived with a broken cold-chain indicator. Lab technician Ms. Pilar Aguirre photographed the indicator, refused the shipment per Section 12.1 of the agreement, notified Tidewater within the required 24 hours, and logged the refusal. Replacement cultures arrived 13 October 2023. COMPLIANT. PART THREE: SUMMARY AND RECOMMENDATIONS. Of the nine findings, eight are COMPLIANT or require no finding, one is NON-COMPLIANT (Finding 2.2, procedural, self-corrected). The review team recommends: (1) that the Lab file all unavailability verification emails with purchasing records going forward; (2) that all data sharing use the project data portal without exception; and (3) that the existing conflict-of-interest management plan be renewed at the next annual disclosure cycle. No referral to the Standing Committee on Research Misconduct is warranted. Signed: R. Nakamura, Director, Office of Research Integrity and Compliance.

NORTHGATE AUTO GROUP - INCIDENT REPORT IR-2290
LOANER VEHICLE PARKING CITATION AND APPEAL REVIEW
Prepared by: Hiro Bergstrom, Service Advisor
Reviewed by: Esi Novak, F&I Clerk
Date of report: February 5

SECTION I - SUMMARY
This report concerns Citation #77341, a Notice of Private Parking Violation issued against a loaner vehicle (2024 silver sedan, VIN ending 8126, registered owner: Foxglove Rentals LLC) that was assigned to service customer Yara Alvarez on January 6 while her own vehicle was in our service bay. The notice was issued by campus security for Larkspur Foods, whose loading zone adjoins our service lot. The question presented is (1) whether Ms. Alvarez is responsible for the citation under the Foxglove rental agreement, (2) whether the late penalty applies, and (3) whether the appeal as submitted satisfies the operator's requirements. For completeness, Appendix C reproduces the vehicle specification sheet for the loaner.

SECTION II - TIMELINE

Jan 3, 8:40 AM - Ms. Alvarez books service for her 2019 hatchback (brake recall and 60k service) for Monday, January 6.

Jan 5, 4:15 PM - Our office requests a loaner from Foxglove Rentals under our floor agreement. Foxglove assigns the 2024 silver sedan. Foxglove's rental agreement, which the renter signs at handover, provides in paragraph 7: "The renter is responsible for all parking citations incurred during the rental term. The rental term begins at the moment the renter signs the handover acknowledgment and receives the keys. Citations incurred BEFORE handover are the responsibility of the party then in custody of the vehicle."

Jan 6, 7:52 AM - Ms. Alvarez arrives. Her hatchback enters our service bay. She declines the loaner at first, saying she will wait in the lounge. The loaner sedan remains parked in our service bay, keys held at our service desk.

Jan 6, 1:05 PM - Larkspur Foods campus security patrol logs a vehicle "silver sedan, no visible occupant, plate SVR-2214, parked adjacent to the loading dock ramp" at the boundary of our lot. The patrol log entry reads: "14:02 - citation #77341 affixed to windshield, plate SVR-2214, unauthorized vehicle in loading zone, fee $85 if paid within 14 days of issue, $40 late penalty thereafter. Registered owner per plate lookup: Foxglove Rentals LLC. Notice to be mailed to registered owner." Larkspur's posted rules state a ten-minute grace period for ACTIVE loading activity; the vehicle was unoccupied and showed no loading activity.

Jan 6, 2:40 PM - Ms. Alvarez's hatchback service is completed. Our bay log shows the loaner sedan was still in our service bay at 2:40 PM; the citation itself was written at 2:02 PM, at which time the loaner had never left our custody and Ms. Alvarez had never driven it.

Jan 6, 3:10 PM - Handover. Ms. Alvarez signs the Foxglove handover acknowledgment and receives the keys. This is the start of her rental term under paragraph 7. Service advisor note: "Customer noticed a folded paper under the wiper as she pulled out; brought it to the desk at 3:25 PM. It was citation #77341, issued 2:02 PM, before she had the keys. I scanned it to her file and told her we would support an appeal. - H. Bergstrom."

Jan 6, 3:26 PM - Citation #77341 logged in our incident register with the scanned copy.

Jan 9 - The citation is also mailed by Larkspur Foods to Foxglove Rentals as registered owner, with a notice that Foxglove may re-bill the renter "if the citation arose during the rental term." Foxglove forwards it to us; we forward a copy to Ms. Alvarez.

Jan 12 - Ms. Alvarez mails her written appeal to Larkspur Foods' adjudication office, postmarked January 12. Envelope contents: (1) the appeal form; (2) a photocopy of citation #77341; (3) our service order showing the loaner was in the dealership's service bay at 2:02 PM on January 6, with the bay log page; (4) the Foxglove handover acknowledgment, signed and timestamped 3:10 PM, showing the rental term began after the citation was issued. She signed the appeal form herself as "renter of record." The appeal form's authorization block states: "Appeals must be signed by the registered owner, OR by the renter of record where the rental company has authorized the renter to act in writing." Mr. Bergstrom's same-day email of January 6 to the adjudication office, copy in file, states: "Northgate authorizes Yara Alvarez, renter of record, to act as our and Foxglove's agent in appealing citation #77341." No $15 filing fee was included with the envelope.

Feb 3 - Larkspur Foods' adjudication office issues its decision: citation #77341 is CANCELLED. The decision letter states: "The citation was issued at 14:02 on 6 January while the vehicle was in the custody of the service facility and before the rental term commenced; responsibility therefore does not pass to the renter under the operator's own handover rule. The cancellation moots any late penalty. The appeal, though not signed by the registered owner, was properly signed by the renter of record under the authorization exception; it was timely, as the postmark of 12 January falls within fourteen days of the issue date of 6 January (day 6 of 14)."

SECTION III - LARKSPUR FOODS ADJUDICATION RULES (EXCERPTS)
Rule 2. Any citation may be appealed in writing within fourteen (14) days of the issue date. A timely postmark satisfies the deadline.
Rule 3. An appeal must include: (a) a copy of the citation; (b) evidence supporting the ground of appeal; (c) a declaration that the appellant has filed no more than one prior appeal with this office within the preceding twelve months; (d) payment of a $15 filing fee, which is WAIVED where the citation was issued to a vehicle not in the appellant's custody at the time of issue.
Rule 4. Appeals must be signed by the registered owner, or by the renter of record where the rental company has authorized the renter in writing.
Rule 7. Where a citation is cancelled after a timely-filed appeal, no late penalty shall be assessed for the pendency period.
Rule 9. An appeal filed by the registered owner is presumed made on the owner's own behalf, not on behalf of a renter, unless the owner states otherwise.

SECTION IV - APPEAL LETTER AS SUBMITTED (TEXT)
"To the Adjudication Office, Larkspur Foods: I, Yara Alvarez, renter of record of the vehicle bearing plate SVR-2214, appeal citation #77341 issued January 6 at 2:02 PM. At the time of issue I had not yet received the vehicle; the handover acknowledgment enclosed is timestamped 3:10 PM, sixty-eight minutes after the citation. The vehicle was in the service facility's bay. I enclose a copy of the citation, the service order and bay log, and the handover acknowledgment. I note for completeness that I appealed a citation to your office last June regarding a different vehicle; I have made no other appeals. I ask that the citation be cancelled and that any late penalty not be assessed. Respectfully, Yara Alvarez, renter of record (authorized in writing per your Rule 4 by Northgate's email of January 6)."

SECTION V - PAYMENT AND PENALTY LEDGER
Citation amount: $85 (payable within 14 days of issue; issue date January 6; 14-day date January 20).
Late penalty: $40, assessed after the 14-day date where the amount remains unpaid and no cancellation has issued.
Ledger entries: Jan 12 - "appeal received, postmarked 12 Jan, fee not enclosed (waiver under Rule 3(d) to be confirmed)"; Feb 3 - "citation cancelled; late penalty not assessed per Rule 7"; Feb 4 - "account closed, balance $0." No payment was ever collected from Ms. Alvarez or from Foxglove Rentals.

SECTION VI - CUSTODY NOTES
Two custodies are relevant and must not be conflated: (1) custody of the vehicle, which at 2:02 PM was with Northgate's service department (keys at the service desk); and (2) responsibility under the rental agreement, which under paragraph 7 attaches to the renter only from handover at 3:10 PM. The citation was directed to Foxglove Rentals only because plate lookups return the registered owner; that is an addressing convention, not an allocation of fault.

SECTION VII - COUNTERPARTY CORRESPONDENCE
Feb 4 email from Foxglove Rentals to our office: "We understand citation #77341 was cancelled. Our re-billing clause against the renter was never triggered because the citation did not arise during the rental term. To be clear, had the citation issued at 3:30 PM rather than 2:02 PM, our position would have been the reverse and we would have re-billed Ms. Alvarez as renter. Please also confirm no further incidents on this unit." Our reply confirmed the cancellation and noted the unit's next scheduled service. Separately, a neighbor business, Saltmarsh Foods, emailed us an unrelated complaint the same week about a delivery van blocking THEIR dock on January 8; that van was a Quill Freight truck and has no connection to this citation, which concerns Larkspur Foods' zone and occurred January 6.

SECTION VIII - STATEMENT OF MS. ALVAREZ (JANUARY 14, PHONE, TAKEN BY H. BERGSTROM)
"I want to be precise: I never moved that loaner before 3:10 PM. I was in your lounge all morning. I did not even know it was a loaner with a ticket on it until I pulled out. I am happy to pay what I owe, but I do not owe this one. I appealed once before, last June, about my own hatchback in a garage on Elm Street - that one was dismissed. I will follow whatever the office decides."

APPENDIX A - BAY LOG EXCERPT (JANUARY 6)
07:52 Customer vehicle in bay 3 (hatchback, Alvarez).
09:30 Loaner sedan SVR-2214 staged in bay 5, keys at service desk.
14:02 [External event per Larkspur patrol log: citation #77341 affixed to loaner windshield.]
14:40 Hatchback service complete; invoice printed.
15:10 Loaner handover acknowledgment signed; keys released to Yara Alvarez.
15:25 Citation brought to desk by customer; scanned; incident register entry 26-0119.

APPENDIX B - CITATION #77341 (SCANNED TEXT)
NOTICE OF PRIVATE PARKING VIOLATION. Issued: January 6, 14:02. Plate: SVR-2214. Registered owner: Foxglove Rentals LLC. Location: loading zone ramp, Larkspur Foods campus. Amount: $85 within 14 days; $40 late penalty thereafter. Appeal per posted rules within 14 days of issue date.

APPENDIX C - LOANER VEHICLE SPECIFICATION SHEET (FOXGLOVE RENTALS FLEET UNIT 4471)
Model year 2024 silver sedan. Engine: 2.0L four-cylinder, 158 hp. Transmission: CVT. Fuel economy: 29 city / 37 highway. Fuel type: gasoline, 87 octane recommended. Cargo volume: 13.2 cu ft. Curb weight: 3,010 lb. Seating: five. Safety suite: automated emergency braking, lane-keep assist, adaptive cruise. Infotainment: 8-inch touchscreen, wireless pairing. Maintenance interval: every 7,500 miles. Registration: Foxglove Rentals LLC, plate SVR-2214. Loaner placard: Northgate Auto Group fleet hanger on sun visor. Tires: all-season 205/60R16. Warranty: powertrain 5 years/60,000 miles. This specification sheet is provided for identification of the unit only and forms no part of any appeal or citation record.

END OF REPORT

questions.notes: Paragraph 7 attaches renter responsibility only from handover at 3:10 PM; citation issued 2:02 PM while the dealership held custody. Ticket addressed to Foxglove as registered owner is an addressing convention.

COURTEOUS INCIDENT POSTMORTEM REPORT PR-2026-014
Subject: In Respect of the Duplicated Settlement Disbursement for Claim CLM-20817 (Meridian Logistics, Inc.)

Prepared by: Viktor Lindqvist, Payments Systems Engineering, Elmford Mutual Assurance.
Kindly reviewed by: Yara Haddad, Chair, Claims Committee; Jonas Alvarez, Senior Adjuster.
Date of report: 24 March 2026. Distribution: internal, with the utmost courtesy; please handle with discretion.

PREAMBLE

We wish most sincerely to open this report with an apology. On 17 March 2026 the settlement disbursement for claim CLM-20817 was, through a combination of failures described below, issued twice. We are deeply sorry for the confusion and extra work this has caused to every party, and we hope this document, for all its length, will be received in the patient and generous spirit in which it is offered.

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

With profound regret, we report the following. The agreed settlement of $186,500.00 for claim CLM-20817 (wind and hail damage at the insured's Corbett Falls distribution depot, loss date 3 February 2026) was disbursed twice in the early hours of 17 March 2026. Of the duplicated $186,500.00, a sum of $151,233.62 was recovered by reversal on 19 March 2026; the remaining $35,266.38 had already been drawn by the insured against restoration works and is being repaid under a schedule agreed, we are thankful to say, without dispute. Separately, and with equal embarrassment, the euro conversion of the disbursement applied a stale currency-conversion factor, leaving the insured approximately EUR 1,825 short; reimbursement is in course with our apologies. This report sets out the timeline (Section 3), the relevant Committee minutes (Section 4), the root cause analysis (Section 5), our findings (Section 6), and corrective actions (Section 7), together with a log excerpt (Appendix A), the relevant policy clauses and amendments (Appendix B), and selected correspondence (Appendix C). We apologise for the length; we found it difficult to be both complete and brief, and we chose completeness, hoping the reader will forgive us.

2. BACKGROUND AND CONTEXT

The policy in question is Commercial Property Form CP-4417, policy period 1 January 2026 through 31 December 2026, covering Meridian Logistics, Inc. at its distribution depot on the Corbett Falls Industrial Estate. The insured's risk manager is Ms. Nadia Delgado, to whom we extend our continued thanks for her unfailing courtesy. The placing broker is Fernbrook Brokerage. The assigned senior adjuster is Mr. Jonas Alvarez. The restoration contractor engaged by the insured is Harbor Studio, whose project lead, Mr. Callum Lindqvist, has been gracious throughout. Temporary equipment has been hired from Quill Rentals, Inc. Elmford operates its claims disbursements on the Bluefin Analytics Payments Hub, version 7.4.2, which is configured under the Courteous Logging Convention v2.1; that convention obliges the platform to phrase its log messages politely, and we apologise in advance for any oddity this introduces into Appendix A.

On 3 February 2026 at approximately 04:12 local time, a windstorm accompanied by heavy hail crossed the Corbett Falls area. The depot's roof membrane was torn over approximately 40 percent of the roof plane, permitting water intrusion into storage bays. The estimated ultimate cost of the loss was $214,000; after negotiation conducted, we are glad to say, entirely amicably, the settlement was agreed on 16 March 2026 at $186,500.00. Per the insured's standing instruction, the disbursement was to be converted to euro and delivered to Meridian Logistics' facility account in Galway; the mechanics of that conversion, and the failure that accompanied them, are described in Sections 5 and 6.

3. TIMELINE OF EVENTS

We set out below the principal events, with such commentary as seemed helpful; where an entry is developed further elsewhere in this report, we have said so politely in parentheses.

4. EXTRACTS FROM CLAIMS COMMITTEE MINUTES

We quote the minutes as recorded; the drafting style is the Committee's own, and we would not presume to improve it.

4.1 Meeting No. 7, 11 March 2026. Present: Ms. Yara Haddad (Chair), Mr. Jonas Alvarez, Ms. Priya Kaur (attending for underwriting), and two further members.

Item 3 — Reserve review. The reserve on CLM-20817 was maintained at $200,000, the Committee expressing its appreciation for Mr. Alvarez's scoping worksheet.

Item 4 — Interim advance. The Committee considered Ms. Delgado's request for an interim advance of $48,000 toward temporary roof works. After careful and good-tempered discussion, the Committee did not withhold its approval; it is not the case that the Committee declined to authorize the interim payment, and the Chair was asked, with pleasure, to convey the Committee's approval to the insured most warmly. Treasury was instructed to release the advance with the Insurer's compliments.

Item 5 — Vote of thanks to the adjuster, carried unanimously.

4.2 Meeting No. 8, 13 March 2026. Present: Ms. Haddad (Chair), Mr. Alvarez, and two further members.

Item 1 — Apologies for absence, received graciously.

Item 2 — Equipment deposit. The insured's request for a $12,400 deposit to Quill Rentals, Inc. for generator hire was regretfully declined. The Committee observed that Section 12 of the policy, as amended, does not treat deposits for the hire of equipment as interim advances, and that it would not be proper to authorize this one notwithstanding. The Committee asked that its sincere regret be conveyed to the insured with every courtesy.

Item 3 — Reserve review. No change; the Committee recorded its continued gratitude for everyone's patience.

5. ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS, CONDUCTED MOST POLITELY

5.1 Overview. The duplication arose from the unhappy concurrence of three conditions: a batch retry that regenerated its idempotency key, a duplicate-payment control that had been switched off by hand, and a logging configuration that made the first two conditions harder to see. We take each in turn, and we take responsibility for all three.

5.2 The batch retry. The nightly settlement sweep NS-0317 encountered a transient connection reset with the clearing partner at 02:11 UTC. The platform's retry logic, in circumstances we now regret deeply, generated a fresh idempotency key for the resubmission. In this configuration it was not impossible for the batch to issue the same disbursement twice; indeed, with great regret, it did. We have said plainly what happened because we believe the reader deserves plainness even from a polite document.

5.3 The disarmed control. The duplicate-payment control, DUP-GUARD-2, correctly identified the resubmission as a suspected duplicate at 02:12 UTC and politely declined it. The control was not left to finish its work: at 02:14 UTC a supervisor override, code SUP-4412, entered under the credentials of Mr. Viktor Lindqvist (who has apologised to the Committee in person and repeats his apology here), disengaged the control entirely. The override was entered under reason code MAINT-DRILL, which was not accurate; no drill was scheduled for that night.

5.4 The clock skew. The two application nodes' clocks were not perfectly aligned: node B trailed node A by seven seconds throughout the period. The batch log's timestamps were consequently not free of skew, and entries from the two nodes interleaved out of order, which made the duplicate harder to see during the night and slower to confirm in the morning. We apologise to Treasury for the extra reconciliation work this caused.

5.5 The conversion factor. The insured's standing instruction requires conversion of disbursements into euro. The platform reads its conversion factor from a table last refreshed on 12 February 2026, which then held 1.0897. On 17 March 2026 the current factor was 1.0782. The stale factor was applied, and the euro amount delivered was, we regret to say, approximately EUR 1,825 less than the current factor would have produced. Reimbursement, with interest and apologies, is in course.

6. FINDINGS, EACH OFFERED WITH RESPECT

The review team adopted the following findings. We number them for clarity, not for emphasis, and we present them as candidly as politeness permits.

F-1 — Duplicated disbursement. A duplicated settlement disbursement of $186,500.00 occurred on 17 March 2026: SETT-CLM-20817-002 duplicated SETT-CLM-20817-001. It is not the case that the platform prevented the second submission; the duplicate-payment control having been disengaged at 02:14 UTC, the batch ran twice.

F-2 — Timestamp skew. The batch log's timestamps were not free of skew. Node B trailed node A by seven seconds throughout 00:00–03:00 UTC on 17 March, and the misalignment is visible in Appendix A wherever both nodes logged the same event.

F-3 — Manual override. A supervisor override, SUP-4412, disengaged DUP-GUARD-2 at 02:14 UTC under the credentials of Mr. Viktor Lindqvist. The control was thereby not left engaged, and the resubmission at 02:14:07 UTC passed without obstruction.

F-4 — Stale conversion factor. The euro disbursement was not unaffected by a stale currency-conversion factor. The table value of 1.0897, dated 12 February 2026, was applied where 1.0782 was current on 17 March 2026, leaving the insured approximately EUR 1,825 short.

F-5 — Notice. We cannot conclude that the insured failed to give timely notice under Section 7 of the policy. The loss occurred on 3 February 2026; written notice was received on 19 February 2026, comfortably within the thirty-day period, which expired 5 March 2026. The Committee wishes it recorded, with gratitude, that the insured's notice on this claim was not untimely. We must, with regret, draw a contrast with the insured's separate motor claim CLM-20943 (loss 28 January 2026; written notice 4 March 2026), where notice was regrettably out of time under the corresponding motor provision; that claim is unaffected by this report and is being handled on its own footing.

F-6 — Execution of Amendment No. 3. It is not the case that Amendment No. 3 was executed without the required countersignature. It was executed on behalf of the insurer by Ms. Priya Kaur, Chief Underwriting Officer, on 26 February 2026, and the countersignature was duly affixed; the amendment is in force. An unsigned working draft bearing the initials "J.A." was superseded and has no force.

F-7 — Fire suppression. The depot's fire-suppression inspection was current at the time of loss; no deficiency was noted, and we record this with quiet relief.

F-8 — Equipment deposit. The Committee's regretful decline of the $12,400 Quill Rentals deposit was consistent with Section 12 as amended; no fault is found with the Committee's decision, which was reached with visible reluctance and impeccable manners.

7. CORRECTIVE ACTIONS, OFFERED HUMBLY

CA-1 — Idempotency keys shall be preserved across retries; the fresh-key behaviour has been removed, with apologies to its author.
CA-2 — Supervisor overrides of payment controls now require a second approver; single-person overrides of DUP-GUARD-2 are no longer possible, and we are sorry it took an incident to teach us this.
CA-3 — Network time discipline has been corrected on node B; clock skew exceeding one second now raises an alert.
CA-4 — The currency-conversion table is now refreshed daily at 06:00 UTC.
CA-5 — Reason codes for overrides are validated against the change calendar, so that MAINT-DRILL can be used only when a drill exists.
CA-6 — A politely worded reminder has been added to the batch close message, asking operators to confirm that exactly the intended disbursements occurred.

APPENDIX B — POLICY CP-4417, RELEVANT CLAUSES WITH AMENDMENTS (EXTRACTS)
(Quoted as issued; we apologise for the legalese, which we have not felt entitled to soften.)

Section 7 — Notice of Loss. "The Insured shall not fail to deliver to the Insurer, or to its designated representative, written notice of any loss covered hereby not later than thirty days following the date of loss. A preliminary verbal notification shall not constitute written notice but shall not prejudice the Insured's rights under this Section. Written notice shall be deemed duly given if posted or delivered electronically so as to be received within the said thirty days. Failure to give written notice within thirty days shall not bar the claim unless the Insurer demonstrates actual prejudice."

Section 12 — Interim Payments. "The Insurer may, in its discretion and upon the recommendation of the Claims Committee, authorize interim advances toward the cost of covered repairs. The Insurer shall not be obliged to authorize any interim advance. Deposits for the hire of equipment shall not constitute interim advances unless the Claims Committee expressly resolves otherwise."

Section 21 — Windstorm and Hail. "Loss caused by windstorm to property in the open is excluded. Hail damage to a roof shall not be excluded where the roof was not more than twenty years old on the date of loss. The deductible applicable to wind and hail loss shall be as set out in the deductible schedule attached, as replaced from time to time by amendment."

Amendment No. 1 (10 February 2026) — Storage subcap removed. "The per-bay storage subcap is deleted in its entirety." Executed for the Insurer by T. Whitfield, former Chief Underwriting Officer; acknowledged for the Insured by Nadia Delgado.

Amendment No. 2 (18 February 2026) — Temporary locations endorsement. "Coverage extends to temporary storage locations within 50 miles for up to 120 days." Executed for the Insurer by Renata Ostrowski, Assistant Underwriter.

Amendment No. 3 (26 February 2026) — Windstorm deductible schedule replaced. "The deductible schedule attached at page 2 of this Amendment replaces, in its entirety, the schedule referred to in Section 21." Executed on behalf of the insurer by Ms. Priya Kaur, Chief Underwriting Officer. For the avoidance of doubt, and recorded with the Insurer's compliments: the executed counterpart retained in the policy file is not unsigned; it is not the case that any attorney-in-fact or delegate affixed the signature in her place; and the Insured's acknowledgment was waived in writing by the Insurer, such waiver being attached at page 3 of this Appendix. An unsigned working draft of this Amendment bearing the initials "J.A." is superseded and has no force.

APPENDIX C — SELECTED CORRESPONDENCE (QUOTED WITH PERMISSION, AND WITH CONTINUED APOLOGIES FOR OUR VERBOSITY)

C.1 — 19 February 2026, Ms. Delgado to the claims inbox: "Dear Elmford team, we write most respectfully to give written notice of the storm loss at our Corbett Falls depot, which occurred on 3 February. Photographs and the broker's preliminary call record are attached. We trust we are not out of time; we believe we are not. With thanks for your kind attention, Nadia Delgado."

C.2 — 24 February 2026, Mr. Alvarez to Ms. Delgado: "Dear Ms. Delgado, thank you for your note of the 19th, which reached us well within the period described in Section 7; your notice was not untimely, and we are grateful for its clarity. I have the honour to be assigned to your claim. Kind regards, Jonas Alvarez."

C.3 — 12 March 2026, Ms. Haddad to Ms. Delgado: "Dear Ms. Delgado, it is my pleasant duty to confirm that the Committee did not withhold approval of the interim advance of $48,000; kindly expect funds tomorrow, with our compliments. We were sorry to learn of the Committee's separate decision on the generator deposit, and we hope you will not think us unkind. Yours most sincerely, Yara Haddad."

C.4 — 20 March 2026, Ms. Delgado to Treasury: "Dear Treasury colleagues, we return $151,233.62 of the duplicated funds today; the remainder was, alas, already spent on Harbor Studio's works, and we will repay it on the schedule we agreed, with thanks for your patience and your good manners. Nadia Delgado."

C.5 — 22 March 2026, internal note, Mr. Alvarez to the motor claims desk: "Re CLM-20943: unlike CLM-20817, where the insured's notice was punctual, the motor claim's notice was, we regret, out of time; please handle the late-notice question under the motor provision, and kindly do not confuse the two claims. Many thanks, J.A."

We close, as we opened, with an apology and a thank-you: an apology for the failure, and a thank-you to everyone whose patience made this report possible.

Hi Yara! Great news — I've located your withdrawal request #W-88231 for 1.25 ETH! Withdrawals typically process within minutes. How is your day going?

---- March 11, 16:30 — Agent (Xiu Castillo) ----
I understand your frustration, Yara. Looking further, I can see that withdrawal #W-88231 has a status flag of "manual review — compliance hold." state:
MERIDIAN DISTRICT RECREATIONAL FLOORBALL & NETBALL ASSOCIATION (MDRFNA)
INTERNAL INCIDENT REPORT IR-2024-117

Subject: Scheduling platform migration failure, fee irregularities, and related matters
Classification: Internal — Distribution List A only
Prepared by: Wanjiru Lindqvist, Honorary Registrar
Reviewed by: Priya Tanaka (Treasurer); Yara Moreau (Fixtures Secretary)
Date of issue: 14 December 2024
Supersedes: none
Retention: 7 years per Records Schedule 12

DISTRIBUTION AND PURPOSE

This report is issued pursuant to Standing Order 4(b) of the Association's Governance Manual, which requires the Registrar to "prepare a consolidated written account of any operational irregularity affecting three (3) or more registered fixtures within a single competition month, for the information of the Executive Committee and for retention in the permanent record." The irregularities described herein arose in connection with the Association's migration of its fixture scheduling, registration and fee-collection functions from the legacy Foxglove Software system ("FGL-League") to the Harbor Software platform ("ScheduleMaster"), together with certain ancillary matters touching on venue management, disciplinary process and equipment rental. The report makes findings of fact only; recommendations appear at Section 8 and do not constitute decisions of the Executive Committee.

SECTION 1. BACKGROUND AND HISTORY

1.1 The Association administers amateur floorball and netball competition for twenty-two (22) registered teams across three divisions, plus a mixed winter social league. Fixture scheduling has, since 2016, been maintained on the Foxglove Software product FGL-League, procured under a licence agreement dated 3 February 2016 (as amended twice, most recently 11 January 2022). Fees, fines and registration payments were recorded in the same system and reconciled monthly by the Treasurer against the association's bank statements.

1.2 During the 2023 close season, the Executive Committee resolved (Minute EC-2023-44) that the Association would "investigate replacement of FGL-League with a modern cloud platform, cost to be capped at the amount provided for in the 2024 budget line 6.2." Three vendors were approached: Harbor Software, Northwind Studio (which quoted for a custom build in partnership with a third-party hosting provider), and Foxglove Software (which offered an upgraded version of the incumbent product). Northwind Studio subsequently withdrew its quotation by letter of 8 September 2023, citing "capacity constraints in the current quarter." Foxglove Software's upgraded quotation exceeded budget line 6.2 by 34 percent and was not pursued further, a fact recorded in the Treasurer's note of 2 October 2023.

1.3 On 15 November 2023 the Association entered into a Software as a Service Agreement with Harbor Software for the ScheduleMaster platform, including the Fixtures Module, the Registration Module, the Fees and Billing Module, and the Notifications Module, together with a maintenance and support contract running for an initial term of twenty-four (24) months from the go-live date. The go-live date was fixed contractually as 1 August 2024. The migration of historical data was subcontracted by Harbor Software to a data-conversion bureau whose identity is not disclosed in the agreement.

1.4 The migration proceeded during July 2024. The Registrar's contemporaneous migration diary records, among other entries: "9 July: fixture list for Div 1 imported. 11 July: Div 2 imported, duplicate venue rows noticed, queried with support. 15 July: Div 3 and social league imported. 19 July: registration database imported; photographs missing; queried. 24 July: fees ledger imported; opening balances spot-checked against June reconciliation; three discrepancies noted, list attached. 29 July: final checks; Northwind Studios' old logo still appearing on printed sheets; cosmetic only. 1 August: live."

1.5 It should be noted for completeness that the Northwind Studio logo appearing on printed fixture sheets was a legacy artefact of the Association's former web design contract with Northwind Studio (2019-2022), and has no connection with the scheduling migration. The logo artefact is documented in bug report HAR-4402 (see Section 5) and is a display issue only.

SECTION 2. RELEVANT RULES AND STANDING ORDERS (EXTRACTS)

2.1 Competition Rule 14 (Fixtures): "The Fixtures Secretary shall publish the fixture list for each division not later than twenty-one (21) days before the first fixture of the season. A fixture may only be postponed or rescheduled with the approval of the Fixtures Secretary, and notice of the revised date shall be published to all affected teams. A fixture which is not commenced for reasons within the control of one team shall be recorded as a forfeit against that team."

2.2 Competition Rule 19 (Rosters and Eligibility): "No player shall appear for a team after the roster freeze date. The roster freeze date for the 2024-25 season is 30 September 2024. Any fixture in which an ineligible player appears shall, upon protest or upon the Registrar's own motion, be recorded as a 5-0 forfeit against the fielding team, subject to appeal."

2.3 Disciplinary Regulation 7.2 (Appeals): "A party wishing to appeal a decision of the Registrar or of a match official shall lodge a written notice of appeal with the Registrar within seven (7) days of the decision, accompanied by the appeal filing fee of $40. An appeal lodged without the filing fee is not validly commenced and shall not be listed for hearing. The appeal filing fee is refunded if the appeal is upheld."

2.4 Disciplinary Regulation 7.4 (Hearing): "The Appeals Panel shall convene within twenty-one (21) days of a validly commenced appeal and shall notify the parties of its decision in writing within seven (7) days of the hearing."

2.5 Standing Order 11 (Venue Bookings): "Venue bookings shall be made through the venue management function of the approved platform. Where two fixtures are allocated to the same venue and time slot, the Fixtures Secretary shall resolve the conflict in favour of the earlier-published fixture and shall reschedule the other fixture with the approval procedure in Rule 14."

2.6 Standing Order 11A (Equipment): "Match equipment supplied under rental arrangements with third parties shall be checked in and checked out by the venue marshal, and any shortage shall be reported to the supplier within 48 hours of the fixture."

SECTION 3. CONSOLIDATED TIMELINE OF EVENTS (AUGUST — DECEMBER 2024)

3.1 3 August 2024. First competitive Saturday of the season. Fixtures published in ScheduleMaster. The Fixtures Secretary notes in her Saturday report that the printed sheet for Division 1 listed the 3 August fixture between Riverside Rockets and Southbank Squalls at "Court 4, Riverside Leisure Centre" while the on-screen schedule showed "Court 4, Riverside Leisure Centre" for a Division 2 fixture between Kingsmere Kestrels and Old Toll Rovers at the same time. The venue marshal at Riverside Leisure Centre telephoned at 09:40 to report that two teams had arrived for Court 4.

3.2 3 August 2024 (later). The Div 2 fixture was stood down and the teams sent home. The Div 1 fixture proceeded. Yara Moreau logged the incident with Harbor Software support as ticket #HAR-4471 (see Section 5) and, separately, recorded a postponement of the Kingsmere Kestrels v Old Toll Rovers fixture "pending rescheduling, date TBC."

3.3 10 August 2024. A second venue conflict occurred at Marsh Basin Sports Hall, where the social league fixture of 10 August was double-booked against a private booking made by Northwind Rentals for a corporate netball event. Northwind Rentals held the confirmed booking; the social league fixture was stood down. The venue marshal's incident slip states: "hall occupied by rental group, boards and posts in use, our slot apparently never confirmed with hall management." Whether the Association's booking was ever validly entered into the hall's own booking system is not established by any document held by the Registrar.

3.4 17 August 2024. The Treasurer, Priya Tanaka, performed the routine monthly reconciliation of the fees ledger in ScheduleMaster against the August bank statement. Her working paper (Appendix A summary) records, among other items, that registration fees received for the Southbank Squalls appeared as $620 in the platform ledger while the bank statement showed a single credit of $590 on 6 August; and that three teams' junior-concession rates had not been applied, so that those teams had been invoiced at the full adult rate. A credit note was raised for the overcharge on the junior concessions on 21 August. The $620/$590 discrepancy was carried as an open query with Harbor Software support (ticket #HAR-4503).

3.5 24 August 2024. The Fixtures Secretary rescheduled the Kingsmere Kestrels v Old Toll Rovers fixture to 31 August, which was published and played without incident. The social league fixture of 10 August was not rescheduled in August; correspondence regarding it appears at Section 6.

3.6 7 September 2024. Roster freeze date under Rule 19. The Registrar's roster freeze instruction, sent to Harbor Software support on 4 September, asked that the Registration Module be configured so that "no player registrations be accepted after 30 September." The support reply of 5 September confirmed the request was "logged as a configuration task for the current sprint." There is no record in the Registrar's files of any subsequent confirmation from Harbor Software that the configuration task was completed.

3.7 14 September 2024. Division 2 fixture: Kingsmere Kestrels v Old Toll Rovers (the rescheduled one). Played at Marsh Basin. During the match, a player listed on the Kestrels' team sheet was challenged by the opposing captain on eligibility grounds. The player had been registered, according to the Registration Module's own audit display, on 4 October 2024 — a date after the roster freeze — although the team sheet was prepared and the match played on 14 September. The apparent inconsistency in the audit display is the subject of bug report #HAR-4512 (Section 5). The match was played to a conclusion (2-2) and the eligibility protest was referred to the Registrar.

3.8 21 September 2024. The Registrar, applying Rule 19, recorded the 14 September fixture as a 5-0 forfeit against Kingsmere Kestrels, the ineligible player having appeared. Written notice of the forfeit decision was sent to both clubs on 23 September. The Kestrels' coach, Farid Haddad, notified the Registrar by telephone on 25 September that the club intended to appeal.

3.9 30 September 2024. The Registrar received by email a written notice of appeal from Farid Haddad, styled "Notice of Appeal against Forfeit Decision of 21 September." The notice of appeal is dated 28 September 2024, sets out grounds in four numbered paragraphs, and requests a hearing before the Appeals Panel. The notice makes no mention of any payment. The Association's published guidance accompanying the appeal form states that the $40 appeal filing fee must accompany the notice; the guidance also notes that appeals may be paid "by bank transfer to the Association's general account, by cheque to the Registrar, or in cash at the pavilion office against a numbered receipt."

3.10 4 October 2024. Registrar's office diary entry: "Farid Haddad appeal — file opened, appeal number AP-24/09. Panel to be convened within 21 days per Reg 7.4 — query whether fee received — asked Priya to check bank statements — she will look when back from leave." There is no subsequent diary entry, bank annotation, receipt stub, ledger line or email in the Association's files showing payment of the appeal filing fee for appeal AP-24/09.

3.11 12 October 2024. Division 1 fixture: Riverside Rockets v Southbank Squalls, Riverside Leisure Centre. The Squalls' captain, Aiden Kaur, submitted a team sheet listing fourteen players; the platform accepted the sheet but the Notifications Module did not send the usual confirmation email to the Registrar's office. This failure is within the known-issue category described in the Harbor Software changelog entry for version 4.1.0 (Section 4) and was reported by the Registrar's office as ticket #HAR-4488.

3.12 19 October 2024. The social league fixture of 10 August was formally recorded by the Fixtures Secretary as "abandoned, not to be replayed," with the entry annotated "per email agreement of 17-19 Oct, see Section 6." The email chain at Section 6 contains proposals and counter-proposals for a replay on 26 October and on 2 November; the chain does not contain any message recording agreement to either date or to the abandonment. The annotation's provenance could not be verified from the correspondence held on file, and the Fixtures Secretary, when asked by the Registrar on 2 December, replied: "I honestly can't reconstruct that entry; it may have come from the old Foxglove habit of auto-closing stale postponed fixtures after 70 days. Can we treat it as a system artefact for now?"

3.13 26 October 2024. Notification from Northwind Rentals to the Association of a claim for unpaid equipment rental in respect of boards and posts supplied for the 3 August and 10 August fixtures at Riverside Leisure Centre and Marsh Basin Sports Hall respectively, in the amount of $310, together with storage charges of $55. The Association's venue marshal's check-out slips for both dates are incomplete: the 3 August slip is signed but records no board count; the 10 August slip is missing entirely because the fixture was stood down.

3.14 9 November 2024. A Division 3 fixture between Old Toll Rovers II and Marsh Basin Mallards at Marsh Basin Sports Hall was abandoned at half-time owing to a floor fault in the south court (a water ingress issue at the venue, unrelated to scheduling software). The score at abandonment was 1-1. Competition Rule 14 does not address mid-fixture abandonment; the Registrar sought the Executive Committee's guidance. The Executive Committee resolved on 13 November (Minute EC-2024-31) that "the abandoned Division 3 fixture of 9 November be replayed at a date to be fixed by the Fixtures Secretary, with the score expunged, venue to be arranged."

3.15 Following the 13 November resolution, the Fixtures Secretary circulated availability inquiries to both clubs. The correspondence is summarised at Section 6.4. As at the date of this report, the fixture remains listed in ScheduleMaster as "REPLAY — DATE TO BE CONFIRMED," and the Registrar's fixture register records the status of that fixture as "replay ordered, date outstanding."

3.16 1 December 2024. Northwind Rentals issued a formal letter before action and, on 5 December, filed a claim in the Small Claims Division of the Local Court against the Association. The filing is summarised at Section 7. The Association's solicitor has been instructed to acknowledge the claim.

SECTION 4. SOFTWARE CHANGELOG EXTRACT (HARBOR SOFTWARE, SCHEDULEMASTER)

The following entries are reproduced verbatim from Harbor Software's public release notes for the Fixtures, Registration and Notifications Modules, as published on the vendor's customer portal. The Registrar downloaded the extract on 6 December 2024. The extract is included here because several of the incidents in Section 3 are traceable to documented platform behaviour.

Version 4.0.9 (released 21 June 2024)
- General stability improvements to the Fixtures Module import pipeline.
- Fixed an issue where imported fixture lists retained the "printed header" image configured in a customer's previous system, causing stale third-party branding on printed sheets. (Ref: customer report HAR-4402.)
- Updated the venue picker to display court numbers in ascending order.

Version 4.1.0 (released 19 July 2024)
- NEW: Venue conflict pre-check at import time. The pre-check compares newly imported fixtures against existing venue bookings within the customer's own ScheduleMaster environment and warns where a conflict is detected. NOTE: the pre-check does not currently compare against bookings held in external venue management systems operated by halls or leisure centres. Cross-system venue booking remains the customer's responsibility.
- KNOWN ISSUE: transactional notification emails (fixture confirmations, team-sheet confirmations, fee receipts) may fail to send when the sending queue reaches more than 500 messages per day. Customers operating large weekend fixture lists may see intermittent non-delivery. Workaround: verify receipt in the audit log. Fix targeted for a later release.
- Improved accessibility of the fees dashboard.

Version 4.1.1 (released 6 September 2024)
- Fixed a rounding error in the Fees and Billing Module that caused junior concession rates to be skipped when a team's registration contained a mixture of adult and junior players, resulting in overcharge at the full adult rate for the junior portion. (Ref: customer report HAR-4503.) Customers who identified affected invoices should issue credit notes manually from the reconciliation screen.
- Fixed a display bug in the Registration Module audit view. Previously, the audit view displayed the "registration accepted" timestamp instead of the "registration submitted" timestamp, which could make validly registered players appear to have been registered after a freeze date. (Ref: customer report HAR-4512.) Note for administrators: this release corrects the display only; it does not retroactively alter any eligibility determination made on the basis of the incorrect display.
- Maintenance release: no new features.

Version 4.1.2 (released 11 October 2024)
- The transactional notification email queue has been re-architected to remove the daily cap described under version 4.1.0. Notification reliability is restored. Customers who relied on the audit-log workaround during the affected period need take no further action.
- Fixed an issue where postponed fixtures auto-closed as "abandoned, not to be replayed" after 70 days of inactivity when migrated from a legacy system whose status vocabulary included a "pending rescheduling, date TBC" state. Migrated fixtures in that state at import time are now mapped to "postponed, rescheduling required" and will not auto-close. Customers whose fixtures were auto-closed between 1 August and the date of this release may reopen them from the fixture history screen. (Ref: internal audit; first reported by a customer on 21 October.)
- The venue conflict pre-check now supports manual entry of external bookings as reference-only records.

Version 4.1.3 (released 29 November 2024)
- Patch release addressing a regression in the printed fixture sheet generator introduced in 4.1.2 (sheet headers could display the previous season's division label). No change to fixture data.
- Documentation update clarifying that the Fees and Billing Module does not record payments received outside the platform (cash, cheque); such payments must be entered manually by an administrator against the ledger. The Registrar's attention is drawn to this clarification in connection with cash receipts at the pavilion office.

SECTION 5. BUG REPORTS AND SUPPORT TICKETS (SUMMARY OF RECORDS HELD)

Ticket #HAR-4402 — Reported 29 July 2024 by Registrar's office.
Summary: printed fixture sheets display Northwind Studio logo from the Association's former website arrangement; cosmetic.
Status: closed as fixed in 4.0.9.
Note: unrelated to the 2024 migration; the logo artefact came from an old print template.

Ticket #HAR-4471 — Reported 3 August 2024 by Yara Moreau (Fixtures Secretary).
Summary: two fixtures allocated to Court 4, Riverside Leisure Centre, at the same Saturday morning slot following data migration. Affected fixture: Kingsmere Kestrels v Old Toll Rovers (Div 2), stood down on the day.
Vendor response (5 August): "The import pre-check flagged no conflict because both bookings were created inside the same migration batch. We have added the batch case to the pre-check backlog. Recommend manual venue review for the first three weeks of your season."
Status at date of report: open (vendor backlog). Not fixed by 4.1.2; the changelog entries in 4.1.2 address the notification queue and the auto-close behaviour, not batched import conflicts.

Ticket #HAR-4488 — Reported 12 October 2024 by Registrar's office.
Summary: team-sheet confirmation emails not delivered; Registrar's office only became aware of the Squalls' team sheet when the marshal phoned. Attribution: the version 4.1.0 daily queue cap known issue.
Status: closed as fixed by 4.1.2; workaround audit-log entries confirmed the sheet had been submitted on time. No fixture consequence.

Ticket #HAR-4503 — Reported 21 August 2024 by Priya Tanaka (Treasurer).
Summary: fees ledger discrepancies; junior concession rates skipped on mixed rosters (overcharge); also a $620 ledger entry against a $590 bank credit for Southbank Squalls registration, cause unknown.
Vendor response (30 August): concession bug confirmed and fixed in 4.1.1; "on the $620 vs $590, we cannot reproduce; the ledger shows a $30 platform convenience fee applied to the invoice. Please confirm whether your agreement includes the convenience fee."
Treasurer's note (2 September): "I have checked the SaaS agreement; it is silent on convenience fees. I have asked Harbor in writing to point to the clause. No reply yet. The $30 is still on the open queries list."
Status at date of report: partially closed; $30 discrepancy remains open; credit notes for the overcharge were issued manually on 21 August 2024.

Ticket #HAR-4512 — Reported 15 September 2024 by Kingsmere Kestrels (through the Registrar's office).
Summary: Registration Module audit view displayed "4 October 2024" as the effective registration date of a player whose team sheet was used on 14 September, causing an eligibility challenge. The display bug (4.1.1) explains the audit display; the underlying registration record, per the module's raw data export of 16 September, shows a submitted date of 12 September 2024, before the roster freeze.
Status: closed as fixed in 4.1.1, with the vendor's administrator note that the display fix does not retroactively alter eligibility determinations. The Registrar's forfeit decision of 21 September (Section 3.8) was made on the basis of the audit display; the raw data export post-dates the decision.

SECTION 6. CORRESPONDENCE EXTRACTS

6.1 Rescheduling of the 10 August social league fixture (extract).

From: Yara Moreau (Fixtures Secretary) — 12 Aug: "All — after Saturday's clash at Marsh Basin we need to find a slot for the social fixture. I can offer 26 October or 2 November, both afternoons, court 2 at the Basin. Preference to the first team to confirm."
Leila Alvarez (captain, Marsh Basin Mallards social side) — 13 Aug: "We can do 26 Oct if it's the afternoon. What about our booked referee fee — does it carry over?"
Yara Moreau — 13 Aug: "Referee fees carry over, yes. I'll pencil 26 Oct pending the other side."
Aiden Kaur (captain, Old Toll Rovers social side) — 14 Aug: "26 Oct is tricky for us, half the team are away for the half-marathon. Is 2 Nov still on the table?"
Yara Moreau — 14 Aug: "2 Nov is possible, I'd need to check the hall. Leave it with me."
No further message appears in the chain until 19 October, when Yara Moreau wrote to both captains: "Following the auto-closure of this fixture in the platform (see below), and given the lateness of the season, I propose we record the social fixture of 10 August as abandoned, not replayed, and move on. Shout if you disagree by Friday." No reply from either captain is held on file. The platform's auto-closure event is described in changelog entry 4.1.2. The Registrar notes that the "per email agreement" annotation in Section 3.12 is not supported by the correspondence held.

6.2 Appeal correspondence (extract).

From: Farid Haddad — 30 Sep: "Please find attached our Notice of Appeal against the forfeit decision of 21 September. We ask that the Appeals Panel consider the raw registration export showing a 12 September submitted date. Happy to attend any hearing. Farid Haddad, coach, Kingsmere Kestrels."
From: Wanjiru Lindqvist (Registrar) — 1 Oct: "Received, thank you. Your appeal has been opened as AP-24/09. The Appeals Panel will convene in due course per Regulation 7.4. Please ensure the appeal filing fee of $40 is lodged if not already done, per Regulation 7.2; an appeal is not validly commenced without it. Please retain any receipt."
From: Farid Haddad — 1 Oct: "Understood. I'll sort the fee this week."
No receipt, bank credit, cheque record, ledger entry or cash-book entry referencing AP-24/09 or a $40 appeal fee from Kingsmere Kestrels is held on file as at 14 December 2024. The Appeals Panel has not convened; the Treasurer's search of the November bank statements (per her note of 2 December: "went through Nov line by line, nothing for $40 or KK") did not identify such a payment. For comparison, the Association's cash book shows that on 1 October 2024 the pavilion office issued receipt #P-1187 for a $40 appeal filing fee in respect of an unrelated umpire-appeal by the Southbank Squalls (appeal AP-24/10), and that appeal was duly listed.

6.3 Northwind Rentals correspondence (extract).

From: Northwind Rentals — 26 Oct: "Our records show boards and posts supplied on 3 August (Riverside) and 10 August (Marsh Basin). Rental per our rate card is $155 per event plus storage where equipment is not checked out the same day. Your 3 August slip is signed but shows no board count; the 10 August slip was never received. Invoice attached: $310 rental plus $55 storage, total $365, payable within 14 days. Please also note our crews were double-committed on 10 August because of your late clash with our corporate booking."
From: Priya Tanaka — 28 Oct: "The 10 August fixture did not proceed; the Association's position is that equipment supplied for a fixture that was stood down should be charged to the party whose booking displaced ours. We are reviewing."
From: Northwind Rentals — 1 Nov: "We hold a confirmed hall booking for 10 August. We have seen no evidence of the Association's booking with the hall. Our invoice stands."
The Association's file does not include any hall booking confirmation for Marsh Basin Sports Hall on 10 August 2024, whether from the venue's own system, from ScheduleMaster, or otherwise.

6.4 Replay of the abandoned Division 3 fixture of 9 November (extract).

From: Wanjiru Lindqvist — 14 Nov: "Both clubs — following EC-2024-31, the 9 November fixture is to be replayed. Please send weekend availability for December and January to Yara by 24 November."
Old Toll Rovers II (team manager, unsigned) — 18 Nov: "We can offer 14 Dec, 15 Dec, or any Saturday in January except 11 Jan."
Marsh Basin Mallards (Leila Alvarez) — 22 Nov: "Our availability is 21 Dec or 4 Jan; we cannot do 14-15 Dec because of the club dinner, and January Saturdays other than 4 Jan look unlikely given holidays."
From: Yara Moreau — 23 Nov: "Noted, thanks. 21 Dec might work — I need to check whether Marsh Basin is free that afternoon given the hall's floor repair. I'll come back to you both once I've spoken to the venue manager."
No further message appears in the chain. Marsh Basin Sports Hall's availability for 21 December is not recorded anywhere in the Association's files. The venue manager was on leave from 25 November to 9 December; whether the Fixtures Secretary spoke to the venue manager upon her return is not documented. The fixture remains shown in ScheduleMaster as "REPLAY — DATE TO BE CONFIRMED."

SECTION 7. COURT FILING EXCERPT (SMALL CLAIMS DIVISION, LOCAL COURT)

Claim no. SC-2024-2819, filed 5 December 2024 by Northwind Rentals Pty Ltd ("the Plaintiff") against Meridian District Recreational Floorball & Netball Association Incorporated ("the Defendant"). Nature of claim: unpaid account for hire of sporting equipment. Amount claimed: $365 plus filing costs of $45.

The Plaintiff's particulars, so far as relevant, state: (a) the Plaintiff supplied boards and posts at Riverside Leisure Centre on 3 August 2024 and at Marsh Basin Sports Hall on 10 August 2024 pursuant to a hire arrangement conducted with the Defendant's venue marshal; (b) the agreed rate was $155 per event; (c) equipment from the 10 August event was not checked out on the day and accrued storage at $5 per day for eleven days, $55 in total; (d) the Defendant has failed to pay the invoiced sum of $365 within the stipulated 14 days.

The Defendant's draft defence, prepared by the Association's solicitor and circulated to the Executive Committee on 11 December (not yet filed), pleads: (a) that the 10 August fixture was displaced by the Plaintiff's own corporate booking, and any equipment supplied for a fixture that did not proceed was supplied to the Plaintiff's event; (b) that the check-out slip regime under Standing Order 11A was not observed by the Plaintiff's crew; (c) set-off in the sum of $30 representing the platform convenience fee under dispute with a third party, which the solicitor's memorandum of 12 December describes as "arguably misconceived, since the $30 is owed to the Association by Harbor Software, not by the Plaintiff." The solicitor's memorandum recommends settling the claim at $365 plus costs. No decision on settlement has been made by the Executive Committee; the matter is listed for directions on 19 January 2025.

SECTION 8. FINDINGS AND RECOMMENDATIONS

8.1 Findings of fact (summary): (a) the 3 August venue conflict arose from a batched-import defect documented in ticket #HAR-4471; (b) the overcharge of junior concession rates arose from a billing defect documented in ticket #HAR-4503 and changelog 4.1.1, for which credit notes were issued on 21 August 2024; (c) the apparent post-freeze registration display was a display defect documented in ticket #HAR-4512; (d) the auto-closure of the 10 August social fixture arose from the legacy-vocabulary mapping defect documented in changelog 4.1.2; (e) notification non-delivery on 12 October arose from the queue-cap known issue documented at changelog 4.1.0 and fixed at 4.1.2; (f) the $30 discrepancy remains an open query with Harbor Software.

8.2 The Registrar notes the interaction between ticket #HAR-4512 and appeal AP-24/09: the forfeit decision of 21 September rests on a display that the vendor has since corrected, and the raw export suggests the player was validly registered before the freeze. The Registrar expresses no view on the merits; the appeal, if validly commenced, is for the Appeals Panel.

8.3 Recommendations: (i) that the Executive Committee consider terminating the maintenance and support contract with Harbor Software under clause 14.3 of the SaaS Agreement (persistent defects); (ii) that a draft termination notice be prepared for the Committee's consideration; (iii) that the September fixture result stand pending the appeal; (iv) that the 9 November replay be scheduled by 31 January 2025; (v) that cash and cheque receipts at the pavilion office be entered against the ledger on the day of receipt, per the vendor's documentation note at 4.1.3; (vi) that the $30 convenience-fee query be pursued in writing.

8.4 Status of recommendations: Recommendation (i) was tabled at the Executive Committee meeting of 12 December 2024. Minute EC-2024-40 records: "Termination of the Harbor Software maintenance contract: DISCUSSION. The Committee noted the draft termination notice circulated by the Registrar. On the proposal of the Treasurer, seconded by the Fixtures Secretary, consideration of termination was DEFERRED to the January 2025 meeting to allow the small claims matter to conclude first. No decision was taken." A draft termination notice, addressed to Harbor Software and dated 10 December 2024, is held in the Registrar's drafts folder marked "HOLD — not sent." No termination notice, notice of intent, or other communication ending or suspending the maintenance contract has been sent to Harbor Software as at the date of this report, and no vendor contract of any kind has been terminated by the Association during 2024. The contracts with Foxglove Software (legacy licence) and Northwind Studio (web design, 2019-2022) ended by expiry in 2022 and 2023 respectively, before the migration, and no current contract exists with either.

APPENDIX A. FEES LEDGER — SELECTED ENTRIES (AUGUST-OCTOBER 2024)

Registration fees received: Riverside Rockets $590 (3 Aug); Southbank Squalls $590 bank / $620 ledger (6 Aug); Kingsmere Kestrels $445 incl. 3 juniors at concession (9 Aug); Old Toll Rovers $590 (10 Aug); Marsh Basin Mallards social $180 (12 Aug).

Hi Chiara, hi Rosa,

OK so this got a bit messy and I want to get everything down in one place before it gets messier, because I've now had THREE different versions of events today and honestly my whiteboard looks like a conspiracy wall. Let me walk through it and you can tell me where I've lost the plot.

So this morning I got the web form submission below -- it came through the 'Student Actions' portal at 8:12am, so it's timestamped, which matters, we'll come back to why it matters. Forwarding it below exactly as received, typos and all.

--- FORWARDED: Student Actions Portal submission ---

Submitted: Tuesday 14 May, 08:12

So, to be crystal clear because this is the part everyone keeps getting wrong: Dmitri submitted this himself. It came from his student account, his login, his words. I did not put him up to it, Rosa did not put him up to it, nobody 'pulled him out of the course'. My role was purely to process it, which I did at about 11:40 the same morning, standard processing, nothing fancy.

Except THEN at lunch Rosa cornered me in the kitchen while I was trying to microwave my soup and said, and I quote, 'I can't believe you dropped Dmitri, that's so unlike you, he was doing so well.' And I said, I did NOT drop him, he dropped himself! And she said 'well that's not what Chiara told me.' So apparently there's a version going around that I initiated the withdrawal, which, no. Absolutely not. I have the form, I have the timestamp, I have the confirmation email I sent Dmitri at 11:47 saying 'processed your withdrawal as requested'. AS REQUESTED. BY HIM.

Also complicating things: there's a second Delgado in the system, Dmitri's cousin Antonia Delgado (ID DG-4488, different person entirely, also a Tuesday student, no relation to the withdrawal, but you can see how the roster mix-up happened, more on that below).

While we're here, the money side, because Dmitri's hardship claim runs into the Copperleaf contract. Extracts below, with both amendments, current as of today:

--- CONTRACT EXTRACT: Catering Services Agreement between Brookfield Adult Learning Centre ('the Centre') and Copperleaf Foods Ltd ('the Supplier'), signed 3 February ---

Clause 7 (Deposits and Payment): The Centre shall pay the Supplier a non-refundable deposit of 400 pounds within 14 days of signature. Thereafter the Centre shall pay the Supplier monthly in arrears for catering supplied to Saturday workshops.

AMENDMENT 1 (executed 28 February, initialed by both parties): Clause 7 is amended such that the deposit shall be 450 pounds, payable within 21 days of signature. All other terms unchanged.

The Supplier shall carry the deposit as an internal credit against the Centre's account and shall not invoice the Centre for it. The Supplier remains responsible for all monthly arrears invoicing as before.

--- END EXTRACT ---

So yes, that's right, the amendment actually flipped who carries the deposit -- I had to read it twice. Not our problem anymore, which is a sentence I don't get to say often, so enjoy it.

Anyway. THEN, this afternoon, Chiara called the meeting, notes pasted below verbatim from my (terrible) live minutes.

CM: Right, agenda item one, Dmitri. Everyone read Uma's email?
